# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Konofal_2014_mazindol"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Konofal_2014_mazindol"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S65495> (open access; PMC4266272)

# Population

Konofal et al. ran an open-label pilot phase II study (NCT00508677) at Robert
Debre Hospital, Paris, in children with attention deficit/hyperactivity
disorder (ADHD) who had responded poorly to methylphenidate. Of the 24 children
enrolled, 21 received mazindol 1 mg orally once daily at 7 am for 7 days
(Table 1). They were 10.7 (SD 1.0) years old (range 9.0-12.8) and weighed
34.9 (SD 9.1) kg (range 27.5-68.0). They were 140.3 (SD 7.6) cm tall, and 19
of the 21 (90.5%) were boys. Race was not reported. Plasma was sampled at 0.5,
2, 4, 6 and 12 h after the first dose and at 12, 24, 36 and 48 h after the
seventh dose. This gave 183 concentrations, 73 of them below the 0.5 ng/mL
lower limit of quantification (LLOQ). The authors fitted the data in NONMEM VI
with the M3 method for below-LLOQ data.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Konofal_2014_mazindol")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Structure: one compartment, first-order absorption with lag, first-order elimination | n/a | Results, 'Pharmacokinetics'; Table 3 |
| `ltlag` (lag time) | 0.3 h, fixed | Table 3; Results ('the value of 0.3 hour was fixed') |
| `lka` (Ka) | 1.02 1/h | Table 3, final model |
| `lcl` (CL/F at FFM 28 kg) | 27.9 L/h | Table 3, final model; Results |
| `lvc` (V/F at age 10 years) | 234 L | Table 3, final model; Results |
| `e_ffm_cl` | 1.24 | Table 3 (theta1); Results equation `CL/Fi = CL/Fref x (FFMi/FFMref)^theta1` |
| `e_age_vc` | 2.28 | Table 3 (theta2); Results equation `V/Fi = V/Fref x (agei/ageref)^theta2` |
| FFM and age reference values | 28 kg, 10 years | Results ('median values of the present population') |
| `etalcl` | 24.5% CV, so omega^2 = 0.0583 | Table 3, final model IIV |
| `etalvc` | 11.4% CV, so omega^2 = 0.0129 | Table 3, final model IIV |
| `addSd` | 0.31 ng/mL | Table 3, 'Residual variability (constant SD)' |
| FFM formula (virtual cohort only) | Janmahasatian, with the sex-specific WHSmax and WHS50 | Methods, 'Pharmacokinetic analysis' |

# Virtual cohort

The study's individual data are not public. The virtual cohort below follows
the Table 1 summaries, with 200 children in a single arm. Covariates come from
base R's random number generator. They are therefore the same on every
machine, unlike the rxode2 random effects.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20141215)
n_sub <- 200

rtrunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  x <- rnorm(n, mean, sd)
  while (any(out <- x < lo | x > hi)) {
    x[out] <- rnorm(sum(out), mean, sd)
  }
  x
}

# Weight is right-skewed (mean 34.9, SD 9.1, range 27.5-68.0 kg): model the
# excess over the 27.5 kg minimum as log-normal with the Table 1 mean and SD,
# truncated at the 68.0 kg maximum.
wt_excess_mean <- 34.9 - 27.5
wt_sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (9.1 / wt_excess_mean)^2))
wt_meanlog <- log(wt_excess_mean) - wt_sdlog^2 / 2
draw_wt <- function(n) {
  x <- 27.5 + rlnorm(n, wt_meanlog, wt_sdlog)
  while (any(out <- x > 68)) {
    x[out] <- 27.5 + rlnorm(sum(out), wt_meanlog, wt_sdlog)
  }
  x
}

# Janmahasatian fat-free mass, with the coefficients printed in Konofal 2014
# Methods (HT in metres).
ffm_janmahasatian <- function(wt, ht_cm, sexf) {
  ht2 <- (ht_cm / 100)^2
  whs_max <- ifelse(sexf == 1, 37.99, 42.92)
  whs_50 <- ifelse(sexf == 1, 35.98, 30.93)
  whs_max * ht2 * wt / (whs_50 * ht2 + wt)
}

cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  AGE = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 10.7, 1.0, 9.0, 12.8),
  WT = draw_wt(n_sub),
  HT = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 140.3, 7.6, 123.1, 153.9),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 2 / 21)
) |>
  mutate(FFM = ffm_janmahasatian(WT, HT, SEXF))

cohort |>
  summarise(
    `Age median (y)` = median(AGE),
    `Weight mean (kg)` = mean(WT),
    `Weight SD (kg)` = sd(WT),
    `FFM median (kg)` = median(FFM),
    `FFM range (kg)` = paste(round(range(FFM), 1), collapse = "-")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Virtual cohort covariates.")

# The paper's reference values are the cohort medians: FFM 28 kg and age 10
# years. A cohort whose FFM median missed 28 kg by several kg would mean the
# FFM formula or the weight/height draws are wrong. The covariates come from
# base R's RNG, so this check is the same on every machine.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(cohort$FFM) - 28) < 3,
  abs(median(cohort$AGE) - 10.5) < 0.5
)
```

The cohort's median age is about 10.7 years, while the paper gives 10 years as
the population median. The Table 1 mean of 10.7 years does not fit a median of
10 years for a roughly symmetric age distribution, and the paper gives no
other age data. The Table 1 summary is used for the cohort. Age enters V/F
with an exponent of 2.28, so in this cohort V/F is centred about 17% above
the 234 L typical value.

# Simulation

Two event tables are used:

* **first dose only**: a single 1 mg dose with dense sampling to 96 h. This
  gives the first-dose Cmax and AUC0-inf that the authors derived from the
  individual post hoc parameters.
* **study design**: seven daily 1 mg doses at 0, 24, ..., 144 h, observed at
  the protocol times (0.5, 2, 4, 6, 12 h and 156, 168, 180, 192 h) plus a
  denser grid for plotting.

```{r events}
make_events <- function(cohort, dose_times, obs_times) {
  doses <- cohort |>
    select(id, FFM, AGE) |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 1, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- cohort |>
    select(id, FFM, AGE) |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

protocol_times <- c(0.5, 2, 4, 6, 12, 156, 168, 180, 192)

ev_single <- make_events(
  cohort,
  dose_times = 0,
  obs_times = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.25), seq(13, 96, by = 1))))
)
ev_study <- make_events(
  cohort,
  dose_times = seq(0, 144, by = 24),
  obs_times = sort(unique(c(
    protocol_times,
    seq(0, 12, by = 0.25),
    seq(144, 192, by = 1)
  )))
)
ev_single$treatment <- "1 mg, first dose"
ev_study$treatment <- "1 mg once daily x 7"
```

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Konofal_2014_mazindol")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20141215)
sim_single <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = ev_single,
  keep = c("treatment", "FFM", "AGE")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_study <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = ev_study,
  keep = c("treatment", "FFM", "AGE")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

## Typical-value check

At the reference covariates (FFM 28 kg, age 10 years), with the random effects
zeroed, a one-compartment model with first-order absorption gives
AUC0-inf = Dose / (CL/F) = 1000 / 27.9 = 35.84 ng*h/mL. Its Cmax and Tmax also
have closed forms. These checks fix the dose-unit conversion and the
parameter transcription.

```{r typical}
typ_ev <- data.frame(
  id = 1L,
  time = c(0, seq(0, 96, by = 0.01)),
  evid = c(1L, rep(0L, 9601)),
  amt = c(1, rep(0, 9601)),
  cmt = c("depot", rep("central", 9601)),
  FFM = 28,
  AGE = 10
)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = typ_ev,
  rtol = 1e-10,
  atol = 1e-12
) |>
  as.data.frame()

ka <- 1.02
ke <- 27.9 / 234
tlag <- 0.3
tmax_cf <- tlag + log(ka / ke) / (ka - ke)
cmax_cf <- 1000 / 234 * ka / (ka - ke) *
  (exp(-ke * (tmax_cf - tlag)) - exp(-ka * (tmax_cf - tlag)))
auc_num <- sum(diff(sim_typ$time) *
  (head(sim_typ$Cc, -1) + tail(sim_typ$Cc, -1)) / 2)
auc_tail <- tail(sim_typ$Cc, 1) / ke

typ_tab <- tibble(
  Quantity = c("Cmax (ng/mL)", "Tmax (h)", "AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)"),
  `Closed form` = c(cmax_cf, tmax_cf, 1000 / 27.9),
  Simulated = c(
    max(sim_typ$Cc),
    sim_typ$time[which.max(sim_typ$Cc)],
    auc_num + auc_tail
  )
)
knitr::kable(typ_tab, digits = 3, caption = "Typical child (FFM 28 kg, age 10 y).")

stopifnot(
  abs(max(sim_typ$Cc) / cmax_cf - 1) < 1e-4,
  abs(sim_typ$time[which.max(sim_typ$Cc)] - tmax_cf) < 0.02,
  # trapezoid on a 0.01 h grid: error well below 0.1%
  abs((auc_num + auc_tail) / (1000 / 27.9) - 1) < 1e-3
)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 5B: visual predictive check

The paper's VPC (Figure 5B) plots the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles of
1,000 simulated replicates over 0-12 h after the first dose and 155-185 h
(12-41 h after the seventh dose), with below-LLOQ values set to 0.25 ng/mL.
The chunk below applies the same summary to the simulated concentrations
including residual error (`sim`). In the published figure the simulated
median is about 2.5 ng/mL at 2 to 4 h. It falls to about 1 ng/mL by 12 h and
is about 1.2 ng/mL at 156 h. These figure readings are approximate.

```{r figure-5b, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
vpc <- sim_study |>
  filter(time <= 12 | time >= 155) |>
  mutate(
    obs = ifelse(sim < 0.5, 0.25, sim),
    window = ifelse(time <= 12, "Day 1 (0-12 h)", "After 7th dose (155-192 h)")
  ) |>
  group_by(window, time) |>
  summarise(
    P10 = quantile(obs, 0.10),
    P50 = quantile(obs, 0.50),
    P90 = quantile(obs, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(window = factor(window, levels = c("Day 1 (0-12 h)", "After 7th dose (155-192 h)")))

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, P50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = P10, ymax = P90), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~window, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (h)",
    y = "Mazindol plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
    title = "Simulated 10th / 50th / 90th percentiles",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5B of Konofal 2014. Dotted line: LLOQ 0.5 ng/mL."
  )

vpc |>
  filter(time %in% protocol_times) |>
  select(-window) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated percentiles at the protocol sampling times.")
```

## Below-LLOQ fraction

The authors report that their model simulated 35% of concentrations below the
LLOQ at the protocol sampling times, against 40% (73 of 183) observed.

```{r blq}
blq <- sim_study |>
  filter(time %in% protocol_times) |>
  summarise(pct_blq = 100 * mean(sim < 0.5))
blq

# The model-true value is about 35% (the authors' own simulation). With
# 200 subjects x 9 samples the between-machine noise is a few points; a
# mis-transcribed CL/F, V/F or a dropped x1000 unit factor moves this by
# tens of points.
stopifnot(abs(blq$pct_blq - 35) < 10)
```

Concentrations at 24 h after the seventh dose (168 h) are reported to range
from below 0.5 to 2.09 ng/mL:

```{r ss24}
sim_study |>
  filter(time == 168) |>
  summarise(
    `median (ng/mL)` = median(sim),
    `P95 (ng/mL)` = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    `% < LLOQ` = 100 * mean(sim < 0.5)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# PKNCA validation

The authors derived first-dose Cmax and AUC0-inf from each child's post hoc
parameters, without residual error. They reported means of 2.99 (SD 0.73)
ng/mL and 32.91 (SD 7.73) ng*h/mL in 20 children (Results, 'Relationship
between exposure, efficacy, and safety'). The comparable simulated quantity
is `Cc`, the individual prediction.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_single |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- ev_single |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0,
  end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE,
  tmax = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE,
  half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published values

The paper reports means, and `ncaComparisonTable()` summarises per-subject
results by the median by default. The simulated results are therefore
averaged by the mean first.

```{r nca-compare}
sim_mean <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(PPORRES = mean(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")

published <- tibble(
  treatment = "1 mg, first dose",
  cmax = 2.99,
  aucinf.obs = 32.91
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_mean,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated mean vs. published mean first-dose exposure. * differs by >20%."
)

pct <- setNames(
  100 * (sim_mean$PPORRES / unlist(published[sim_mean$PPTESTCD]) - 1),
  sim_mean$PPTESTCD
)
# Centre statistics of a 200-subject cohort; a transcription or unit error
# moves either one by tens of percent.
stopifnot(all(abs(pct) < 15))
```

```{r nca-summary}
as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(PPORRES),
    sd = sd(PPORRES),
    median = median(PPORRES),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated first-dose NCA, all parameters.")
```

Simulated mean Cmax and AUC0-inf are within about 10% of the published means.
Simulated AUC runs a little high. Two things push it up. The virtual cohort
truncates weight at the 68 kg maximum, so it has fewer high-FFM (and
therefore high-clearance) children than the study's skewed weight
distribution. And the log-normal IIV on CL/F raises the mean AUC about 3%
above the typical-value AUC, since exp(omega^2 / 2) = exp(0.058 / 2) = 1.03.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV scale.** Table 3 reports between-subject variability as a percentage
  for an exponential model. It is read as a log-normal CV, so
  omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2). At 24.5% and 11.4%, the alternative reading
  omega = CV/100 differs by less than 3% in omega^2.
- **Below-LLOQ handling.** The authors fitted with the M3 likelihood. The
  packaged model carries the additive residual error only; censoring is a
  property of the estimation data, not of the structural model.
- **FFM formula.** The paper applies the adult Janmahasatian formula to
  9-12.8-year-old children, without a paediatric correction. The same
  formula is used here to build the virtual cohort. Users who pass FFM from
  another equation will shift CL/F by (ratio)^1.24.
- **Covariate distributions.** Age, weight and height are drawn independently
  from the Table 1 means, SDs and ranges, and sex from the 2/21 female
  fraction. Truncating the log-normal weight excess at 68 kg gives a weight
  SD of about 4 kg rather than the published 9.1 kg. The published SD
  reflects a few heavy children, up to 68 kg, whom the truncated draw rarely
  reproduces. The cohort's median FFM still matches the paper's 28 kg
  reference. In reality the covariates are correlated (the paper reports a Spearman
  correlation of 0.706 between FFM and age). The paper's own
  reference-population median age of 10 years sits below the Table 1 mean of
  10.7 years. The cohort follows Table 1.
- **Typographical errors in the source.** The Methods print the FFM formula
  as 'FEM', and the Discussion prints the FFM range 22.9-47.2 with the unit
  'kg/m2'. Both are read as FFM in kg.
- **Errata.** No correction notice was found for this article as of
  2026-11-23.
